retrieval_notes: Added 2026-07-06. Galdieria yellowstonensis is a thermoacidophilic red alga formally described by Park et al. 2023 (J. Phycol. 59:444-466, DOI 10.1111/jpy.13322), which places it in the thermoacidophilic Galdieria lineage (order Galdieriales). SAG culture collection entry (SAG:108.79, https://sagdb.uni-goettingen.de/detailedList.php?str_number=108.79) explicitly states: "requires low pH (2-4) and prefers higher growth temperature (25°C, up to 55°C)." Kristijarti et al. 2024 (J. Appl. Phycol. 36:3199-3207, DOI 10.1007/s10811-024-03353-4) explicitly calls SAG 108.79 a "primitive photosynthetic thermoacidophile." Isolated from an acid (pH 3-4) hot spring in Yellowstone National Park, Wyoming (collected 2017-06-02). Kristijarti et al. 2024 Materials and Methods explicitly states: "The Galdieria strains were grown in Allen medium (Allen 1959) at pH 2 with 3% glycerol (v/v) at 40°C, in the dark, and at 150 rpm" — this covers strain 108.79 directly and constitutes a primary-source cultivation temperature of 40°C at pH 2.0. The same paper's introduction states the genus has "adapted to grow at temperatures as high as 55°C." OGT stored as 45°C (conservative: explicit cultivation at 40°C + documented growth up to 55°C supports OGT in the 45-55°C range, consistent with thermoacidophilic classification; no standalone growth-optimum curve paper was found). pH optimum stored as 2.0 (explicit from Kristijarti 2024 cultivation conditions; SAG documents growth range pH 2-4). STRAIN: 108.79 E11 is the genome-sequenced sub-clone; SAG:108.79 is the culture-collection alias. FORMER NAMES: previously deposited in SAG as Cyanidium caldarium and Galdieria sulphuraria (Galdieri) Merola 1982; reassigned to G. yellowstonensis by Yoon, Park et McDermott 2023. Assembly GCA_026122205.1 (ASM2612220v1, Contig, 285x, Sungkyunkwan University 2022; annotation added 2024-01-05) has 7,022 protein-coding genes. FTP protein FASTA verified 200 OK on 2026-07-06. Polarella glacialis CCMP1383 is a psychrophilic Antarctic sea ice dinoflagellate (Dinophyceae, Alveolata) isolated from the ice edge at McMurdo Sound, Ross Sea, Antarctica in June 1991 (Montresor, Procaccini & Stoecker 1999, J. Phycol. 35:186-188). Stephens et al. 2020 (BMC Biology 18:57, PMID 32448240, PMC7245778) is the genome paper and explicitly describes P. glacialis as a 'psychrophilic (cold-adapted) free-living species,' with CCMP1383 as the Antarctic isolate from the Ross Sea and CCMP2088 as the complementary Arctic isolate from Baffin Bay. TEMPERATURE CAVEAT: no formal optimum growth temperature (OGT) from a dedicated growth-curve experiment was found. The NCMA culture collection record (https://ncma.bigelow.org/CCMP1383) lists Maintenance Temperature 2°C and Known Temperature Range 0-6°C; this constitutes explicit culture-temperature evidence from a citable primary culture collection, consistent with the <=15°C psychrophilic threshold. ogt_celsius is stored as 2 (NCMA maintenance temperature, not a formal measured OGT), following the same documentation convention used for Chlamydomonas sp. UWO 241 in this tracker. GENOME: GCA_905237085.1 (Pgla_CCMP1383, NCBI reference genome, Scaffold, University of Queensland 2021; BioProject PRJEB33539) has 58,229 protein-coding genes; annotation confirmed (genbank_has_annotation, has_annotation). Genome was generated from a single-cell amplified library. FTP protein FASTA verified 200 OK on 2026-07-06. LINEAGE NOTE: Polarella glacialis is the only dinoflagellate (Alveolata) in this tracker; it adds a completely new supergroup to the psychrophilic set alongside the existing Chlorophyta (C. subellipsoidea, UWO 241) and Bacillariophyta (F. cylindrus) psychrophiles.
